main_body: Shrine-style hall: a large green tile hip roof (rows 4-42) over a red lintel beam, a cream wall with red posts and a dark lattice door, and a stone plinth
top_band: Center column: gold ornaments rows 0-3, light teal ridge/cap band rows 4-8, then the tile roof slope (mid greens, with light tile highlights) rows 9-42; this slope is a large foreshortened top surface
evidence: The roof is drawn as a big tiled slope with a lighter ridge band on top, like the reference house roofs. Under it come the orange lintel beam (rows 43-46) as a distinct front edge, then the vertical wall face (rows 47-73) and the stone plinth. The posts stand proud of the wall and the door lattice is darker and set between the posts. There is no real dark eave shadow band under the roof, but the roof slope plus the front face clearly give both a top surface and a front. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The roof is rich: about 5-6 greens with per-tile highlights, and the dark outline beside it leans purple-brown or green rather than black. The lower half is much thinner. The cream wall panels are big areas (roughly 10x8 px or more) of one flat colour with only a few sparse speckle dots, whereas the references have plaster speckle all over. The posts have 3 tones and the stone plinth is a few flat greys. Tiles in the lower half carry about 2-5 colours, below the reference's roughly 10 per tile. Next to the references the wall looks flatter and thinner.
